## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

# Release & Hotfix Branch Rules

**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.

See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.

## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)

To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.

## Release Branch Behaviour

When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.

**Before writing any code, always:**
1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.

**Allowed on release branches:**
- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch

**Not allowed on release branches:**
- New features or scope additions not in the release
- Refactoring
- Dependency changes
- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches

**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**

The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.

```bash
# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description

# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
```
The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

| `main` | PROD (MRT Production) | Manual | Release manager approval, post-canary smoke |
| `hotfix/*` | PROD (expedited) | Merge to `main` | Abbreviated pipeline, approval gate retained |

GitHub Environment secret scope
-------------------------------

| GitHub Environment | Secrets scoped | Requires reviewer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `staging` | Dev credentials | No |
| `sit` | SIT credentials | Yes — Zimmermann environment owner |
| `pre-prod` | Pre-prod credentials | Yes — Zimmermann environment owner |
| `uat` | UAT credentials | Yes — Zimmermann stakeholder |
| `production` | PROD credentials | Yes — Release manager |

SIT secrets must be scoped to the `sit` GitHub Environment only — they must not be accessible to the `production` environment workflow.

Open dependencies
-----------------

1. **NewStore notification channel** — the deploy-SIT path currently only echoes to the Actions log on success. Wire to Slack webhook, email, or Jira comment once NewStore confirms their preferred channel.
2. **MuleSoft contract test spec source** — `test:contracts` is a placeholder. MuleSoft must publish OpenAPI specs (or expose a contract endpoint in SIT) before the contract gate is active. {
  "metadata": {
    "id": "335216656",
    "title": "Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)",
    "type": "page",
    "created": "",
    "updated": "",
    "url": "https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656",
    "space": {
      "key": "SFCC",
      "name": "Adobe SFCC"
    },
    "version": 18,
    "attachments": [],
    "content": {
      "value": "**Draft proposal** — for review by squad leads + Integration lead before this replaces anything in AGENTS.md or the existing Branching Guide. Prepared by Claude Code, 2026-07-16, on `chore/read-me-cicd-updates`.

Decisions made so far
---------------------

| Decision | Made |
| --- | --- |
| Release cadence: cut a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch every sprint | 2026-07-16 |
| Pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at 0); `v1.0.0` is reserved for go-live | 2026-07-16 |
| `Test` gets its own automated CI gate, modeled on SIT Gate — not manual-only | 2026-07-16 |
| Tag protection, the version-guard check, and Release-per-final-tag are adopted immediately — not phased in later | 2026-07-16 |

The problem with today's model
------------------------------

Only **Dev** is continuously tied to `develop` (deploys on every merge) — that part is fine, it's meant to be the shared integration environment. But SIT/UAT/Stage/Prod are promoted by pointing a workflow at a **branch or tag ref** (`workflow_dispatch` with a `ref` input). In practice this breaks down two ways:

1. **PR branches don't survive.** Once a story's PR merges to `develop`, its branch is typically deleted. There's nothing left to point a later deploy at — you'd have to keep branches alive indefinitely just to remember what shipped where, which doesn't scale past a couple of people.
2. **Environments get forced into lockstep.** If Test, SIT, and UAT all deploy the *same* release branch as it exists right now, they can't run independent testing cycles — a fix landed for UAT is *also* now sitting on whatever branch Test/SIT were pointed at, even if those teams haven't finished their own pass yet.

The fix: promote immutable tags, not floating branches
------------------------------------------------------

This is standard GitFlow practice that's currently missing here: **when a batch of work is ready to test, tag it. Every environment deploys a specific tag, never "whatever's on a branch right now."**

* Tags are **immutable and permanent** — `v0.1.0-rc.1` always means exactly one commit, unlike a PR branch that gets deleted on merge.
* Each environment can sit on a **different tag at the same time** — Test can be validating `v0.2.0-rc.1` while SIT is still working through `v0.1.0-rc.3` and UAT is signing off `v0.1.0-rc.2`. That's what actually decouples the environments' cadences from each other.
* **No new tooling required.** Every `deploy-*.yml` workflow already takes a `ref` input via `workflow_dispatch`, and `git checkout` doesn't care whether `ref` is a branch name or a tag name. The gap today is process (nobody's cutting tags), not infrastructure.

Tag naming convention
---------------------

Matches this repo's existing `release/v{version}` branch convention (see `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`'s own `release/v0.1.0` example) and standard SemVer.

| Tag pattern | Meaning | Example | Points at | Who creates it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.<N>` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, not yet final. Cheap to cut, iterate freely. | `v0.1.0-rc.1`, `v0.1.0-rc.2` | A commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | Any developer |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate. This is what actually promotes through UAT → Stage → Prod. | `v0.1.0` | The `release/vX.Y.Z` commit being merged to `main` | Release manager / tier-1-approver only |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.<N>` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal release train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | A commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | Release manager / tier-1-approver only |

**X.Y.Z meaning:** **X** (major) — breaking change or major milestone (e.g. a new region launch), rare. **Y** (minor) — new stories/features, the normal per-release bump. **Z** (patch) — bug-fix-only releases / hotfixes.

**Pre-launch: MAJOR starts at** `0`**.** SemVer explicitly reserves `0.y.z` for initial development ("anything MAY change at any time"), which fits this project's current phase exactly. Cut one release per sprint as a MINOR bump — sprint 1 is `v0.1.0`, sprint 2 is `v0.2.0`, and so on. PATCH within an already-cut sprint version still means bug-fix-only, same as post-launch. `v1.0.0` **is reserved for go-live** — the first time MAJOR moves off `0` — after which MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning.

### Anatomy of a tag — `v0.1.0-rc.2` broken down

| Part | Name | Meaning | Increments when... |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | Prefix | Not a version number itself — a literal marker so the tag is unambiguously "a version" and `git tag -l 'v*'` filters cleanly. Not part of SemVer itself, but near-universal on git tags. | Never changes |
| `0` | **MAJOR** | Breaking change or major milestone. Locked at `0` pre-launch (see note above) — `1` at go-live, then rare thereafter. | At go-live (→1), then only for a new region launch, a checkout-flow replatform, or anything severe enough that every in-flight release branch would need to rebase against it |
| `1` | **MINOR** | A normal release — new stories/features, backward compatible | Every sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut from `develop` |
| `0` | **PATCH** | Bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped MAJOR.MINOR | A hotfix after `v0.1.0` has already shipped → the next one is `v0.1.1`, not a new minor |
| `-rc.2` | **Pre-release identifier** | "Release candidate" — this specific build is being validated, not yet final. The number is a simple incrementing counter, not an environment reference. | Each time a fix lands and a new candidate build is cut for the same target version |

The `-rc` number does **not** correspond to an environment — the same `v0.1.0-rc.1` tag can be deployed to Test today and SIT tomorrow. Which environment tested which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s GitHub Actions run history, not the tag name. The only other pre-release suffix in this scheme is `-hotfix.<N>` (same pattern, cut from `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` instead of `release/vX.Y.Z`). No suffix at all (plain `vX.Y.Z`) means final, shipped.

**Why the dot before the number (**`-rc.2`**, not** `-rc2`**):** SemVer pre-release identifiers compare numerically only when they're separate dot-separated fields. `rc.10` and `rc.2` compare correctly as numbers (10 > 2). `rc10` and `rc2` compare as one string each and sort alphabetically — `rc10` would incorrectly sort *before* `rc2`. This matters directly for the safe-upward-deploy check below.

Flow
----

wide4000nonedevelop ──● story A merges
●
● story B merges ─┐
● │ sprint ends → cut release/v0.1.0
●───────────────────release/v0.1.0
│
● tag v0.1.0-rc.1 ──▶ deploy to Test (Test gate must pass before promoting further)
│
(Test gate passes, or a fix/release-v0.1.0-\* PR lands a fix)
│
● tag v0.1.0-rc.2 (if a fix landed) ──▶ deploy to SIT
│
(SIT signs off, on NewStore's own cadence — doesn't block on UAT/Stage)
│
● tag v0.1.0 (final candidate) ──▶ UAT
│
(Business sign-off)
│
● same tag v0.1.0 ──▶ Stage (booked 2-week E2E window)
│
(Contractual perf/E2E sign-off)
│
merge release/v0.1.0 → main, tag v0.1.0 on main too,
back-merge → develop (per existing GitFlow rules)
│
▼
Prod (release manager + canary gate)

**Invariant this model depends on:**`main` always reflects exactly what's live in Prod — nothing merges to `main` except a final tag that has actually passed Stage and been deployed. **Multi-region rollout** (AU canary → flag-flip to remaining regions, per `architecture.md`'s Prod row) is controlled by feature flags within a single deployed version, not by separate per-region tags or deploys — this model deploys one version everywhere; regional exposure is a flag concern, not a tagging concern.

> YellowUpdated — review **Correction (review, 2026-07-18):** the SIT step in this diagram assumes `deploy-sit.yml` becomes tag-triggered. That is **not how it works today** — its real trigger is `workflow_run` off `SIT Gate` completing on a `release/**` branch push, with no relationship to tag creation at all. Treat the SIT step above as the proposed target state, not current behaviour, until Open Question 3 below is decided.

The Test gate
-------------

Decided: `Test` gets its own automated CI gate, not a manual-only tier. Its trigger shape is different from SIT Gate's, though, so the mechanics need to differ too:

* **SIT Gate (**`digital-sit.yml`**) runs** ***before*** **deploy** — triggered on push/PR to a `release/**` branch, and `deploy-sit.yml` only fires once that gate workflow completes successfully.
* `Test` **has no such push/PR event to hang a pre-check on** — it's deliberately on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`), including deploying arbitrary feature branches for a quick look before any release branch exists at all.

**Proposed shape:** run the gate *after* the deploy, as a second job in the same `deploy-test.yml` run — deploy first (the on-demand action stays fast and simple), then immediately run a lighter P0-only Playwright suite against what was just deployed. The workflow run's overall pass/fail becomes the promotability signal: a green run means this tag is safe to push on to SIT; a red run means it isn't, without blocking the ability to trigger a look in the first place. This intentionally skips the bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse checks SIT Gate also runs — those matter more once something's headed toward Stage/Prod, not for an early single-story look.

This is a design proposal, not yet built — flag if you want it modeled differently (e.g. gate-before-deploy to match SIT exactly, at the cost of losing the fast on-demand deploy).

How to deploy to a specific environment
---------------------------------------

All five `deploy-*.yml` workflows (`test`, `sit`, `stg`, `uat`, `prod`) already take a `ref` input via `workflow_dispatch` — this proposal changes what value you put there (a tag, not a branch), not the workflow itself. `Dev` stays fully automatic (every merge to `develop`). Tags are cut with `npm version` (built into npm) rather than raw `git tag` — it bumps `package.json`'s version and creates a correctly-formatted **annotated** tag in one step, so nobody has to remember the naming rules or the `-a -m` flags by hand. See Tagging management strategy below for why annotated tags matter.

### 1. Cut a release branch at the end of each sprint

wide4000bash
git checkout develop && git pull
git checkout -b release/v0.1.0
git push -u origin release/v0.1.0

### 2. Cut the first release candidate and deploy it to Test (or SIT)

wide4000bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0
# First rc of a pre-launch sprint release -> preminor (MAJOR stays locked at 0).
npm version preminor --preid=rc -m "Release candidate %s"
# package.json is now 0.1.0-rc.0, an annotated tag v0.1.0-rc.0 was created, and a
# "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0" commit was added on this branch.
git push origin release/v0.1.0 --follow-tags
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
# once the Test gate passes, same tag (or the next rc) goes to SIT
gh workflow run deploy-sit.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0

### 3. A problem is found — fix, re-tag, re-deploy just the environment that needs it

wide4000bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-checkout-bug
# ...make the fix, open a PR targeting release/v0.1.0, get it merged...
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull
npm version prerelease --preid=rc -m "Release candidate %s" # 0.1.0-rc.0 -> 0.1.0-rc.1
git push origin release/v0.1.0 --follow-tags
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.1 # re-deploy wherever needed — SIT is untouched if it's still on rc.0

### 4. Every rc has signed off — cut the final tag and promote it through UAT → Stage → Prod

wide4000bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0
npm version 0.1.0 -m "Release %s" # strips the -rc.N suffix explicitly — npm has no automatic "graduate" verb
git push origin release/v0.1.0 --follow-tags
gh workflow run deploy-uat.yml -f ref=v0.1.0
# after Business sign-off:
gh workflow run deploy-stg.yml -f ref=v0.1.0
# after the Stage E2E window signs off, merge to main:
git checkout main && git merge --no-ff release/v0.1.0
git push origin main
gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0
# back-merge per existing GitFlow rules (.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md)
git checkout develop && git merge --no-ff release/v0.1.0
git push origin develop

### 5. Rollback — not a special case

If a tag deployed to Prod turns out to be bad, there's no separate rollback mechanism to build — just redeploy the previous known-good tag:

wide4000bashgh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.0.1

Tracking deployments & safe upward promotion
--------------------------------------------

How do we know what's currently live in each environment, and how do we stop someone accidentally deploying an older tag over a newer one?

| Concern | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| **What's deployed where, right now** | Already tracked for free. Every `deploy-*.yml` job is bound to a real GitHub `environment:`, so GitHub automatically records a Deployment each run — visible at Settings → Environments → `<tier>` → Deployments, or `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=sit`. This exists today; it's just not surfaced anywhere visible to the team yet. |
| **Preventing an accidental downgrade** | Add immediately (see Decisions above): a version-guard step to each `deploy-*.yml`, before the push step — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via the Deployments API above, semver-compare it against the tag being deployed, and fail on a downgrade. Use the `semver` npm package for the comparison rather than hand-rolled bash string comparison — see the `-rc.2` vs `-rc2` note above for exactly the class of bug that produces. **Use the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; this exact mismatch already bit this repo once, see `deploy-stg.yml`'s fix history). Map each tier to its real Environment name explicitly, and fail closed on an unresolvable environment/API error — as opposed to a genuine first-ever deployment with no prior Deployment record at all, which should be allowed to proceed. |

Tagging management strategy
---------------------------

| Concern | Recommendation |
| --- | --- |
| **Who can create a tag?** | `-rc` tags: any developer — they're cheap, iterative, and low-risk. Final `vX.Y.Z` and `-hotfix` tags: release manager / tier-1-approver only — mirrors the existing tier-1-approver gate pattern already used for `npm run env -- push` and Contentful config writes. |
| **Ensuring consistency** | Use `npm version` (see "How to deploy" above) instead of hand-typing `git tag` — it's a standard, built-in npm command that enforces correct SemVer formatting and bumps `package.json` in the same step, so the two never drift. Primary enforcement is the GitHub Rulesets described in the "Tag protection" row below, which genuinely hard-block a non-matching tag at push time on GitHub.com. A `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow is worth keeping too, as defense-in-depth and for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives. |
| **Tracking who created a tag** | `npm version` creates **annotated** tags by default (never lightweight ones) — the tagger's identity, timestamp, and message are embedded directly in the tag object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.2` reveals it). This is why the commands above always pass `-m`. |
| **Avoiding tag name conflicts** | Mostly already solved by git itself: `git push origin <tag>` fails outright if that tag already exists on the remote — there's no silent overwrite without an explicit `--force`, which the tag-protection rules below block for anyone but repo admins / tier-1-approvers. `npm version prerelease` also always reads the *current* `package.json` version before incrementing, so it can't produce a number that's already been used on that branch. |
| **Interaction with existing tagging tools** GreenNew — review | Two existing tagging mechanisms predate this proposal and need an explicit resolution, not a silent replacement. `scripts/tagRelease.sh` — the tool the current Branching Guide already prescribes — creates a different tag pair (`v{version}` + `release/digital/v{version}`) via raw `git tag`, run from `main` after a release PR merges; it has no `-rc` concept and conflicts directly with the `npm version`-based flow above. **Recommendation: retire** `tagRelease.sh` **once this proposal is approved** — through the normal script-deprecation process, not a silent deletion. Separately, `deploy-dev.yml`'s `tag-sprint` job pushes `sprint/{sprint}/{date}` tags on every `develop` merge that touches `scripts/sprint.txt` — a distinct namespace (not `v*`) tracking sprint rollover, not release promotion. **No conflict — this coexists unchanged**, since the tag-naming Rulesets below only target `v*`. |
| **Tag protection & naming enforcement** YellowUpdated — review | Adopted immediately (see Decisions above), but as **two separate GitHub Rulesets**, not one — confirmed against GitHub's own Ruleset docs that a single ruleset has only one bypass list for its whole target pattern, so it cannot grant open `-rc` creation to any developer while simultaneously restricting final/hotfix creation to tier-1-approvers. **Ruleset A** targets `v*-rc.*` (tag name pattern `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$`) with "restrict updates" and "restrict deletion" enabled for immutability, and creation left open to any developer with write access — no bypass list needed. **Ruleset B** targets `v*` excluding `-rc.*` (via the ruleset's include/exclude-by-pattern conditions; tag name pattern `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`) with "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled, bypass list scoped to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. Together the two rulesets give the same "newer and more capable than the old tag-protection-rules UI, works on GitHub.com" guarantee as the original single-ruleset design — just correctly split the way GitHub actually requires. |
| **When to tag** | Only at a real promotion gate (about to deploy somewhere), never automatically per-commit — otherwise the tag list becomes as noisy as the commit log and loses its value as a promotion record. |
| **Retention — do we ever delete old tags?** | Keep everything, indefinitely. Tags cost nothing to retain and deleting them destroys the audit trail this whole model is built on ("what was actually deployed to SIT on this date"). If the tag list ever becomes genuinely unwieldy, revisit — don't pre-optimise for it now. |
| `package.json` **version field** | Currently static at `0.0.1`. Under this proposal it tracks the current sprint's release automatically, since `npm version` writes it as part of cutting every tag — no separate bookkeeping needed. |

Rules & automation for AI-assisted development
----------------------------------------------

This project is heavily Claude-Code-assisted, so the convention needs to hold up even when an AI agent (not just a human) is the one cutting a tag. Two layers, not interchangeable:

| Layer | What it does | How reliable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Guidance** — a new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or folded into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*` branches per AGENTS.md) | Documents the convention and tells Claude explicitly to use `npm version`, never construct a `git tag` string by hand | Best-effort — shapes behaviour, but depends on the rule having actually been loaded and followed |
| **Enforcement** — the tag-naming GitHub Ruleset, the `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow, and the Test-gate job (see above) | Runs server-side regardless of who or what pushed the tag / triggered the deploy | A real guarantee — catches a mistake even if the guidance was never read |

The final/hotfix tag gate should reuse the exact `isTier1Approver()` pattern already implemented in `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` — the same trust boundary already used elsewhere in this repo, and one Claude sessions here already know how to check (`gh api orgs/ZimmermannAU/teams/tier-1-approvers/members`).

Per-environment summary
-----------------------

| Environment | What it deploys today | What it would deploy under this proposal | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Local** | `npm start` against your working tree | *(unchanged)* | — |
| **Dev** | Every merge to `develop` | *(unchanged — this is correct as-is, it's meant to be the noisy shared integration tier)* | Auto-deploys on every `develop` merge |
| **Test** *(new —* `deploy-test.yml`*)* | N/A — didn't exist | A feature/fix branch, or an early `-rc` tag, deployed on demand — gated by its own P0-only CI check (see "The Test gate" above) before promoting further | `ref: v0.1.0-rc.1`, or even a raw feature branch for a quick look before a release is cut at all |
| **SIT** YellowUpdated — review | Whatever's on the `release/**` branch when the SIT Gate workflow completes (`deploy-sit.yml` is `workflow_run`-triggered off SIT Gate, not tag-triggered) | A specific `-rc` tag, re-deployed only when a new `-rc` is cut — ***not yet true**, requires a* `deploy-sit.yml` *trigger change from* `workflow_run` *to a tag push; see Open Question 3* | `ref: v0.1.0-rc.2` *(target state, pending decision)* |
| **UAT** | Manual, arbitrary branch/tag | The release's final candidate tag | `ref: v0.1.0` |
| **Stage** | Manual, arbitrary branch/tag | Same tag UAT is validating, once UAT signs off | `ref: v0.1.0` |
| **Prod** | Manual, arbitrary branch/tag | The tag that passed Stage, pushed to `main` | `ref: v0.1.0` |

Changelogs and GitHub Pages
---------------------------

GitHub Pages is enabled on this repo but has never successfully deployed (confirmed via the API — `status: null`). The only thing currently wired to publish there is `digital-sit.yml`'s Playwright-report job. That matters here because `actions/deploy-pages` is a **single-site-per-repo** model — each deployment fully replaces the previous one. A changelog page and the Playwright report can't both live on Pages independently; they'd need to be combined into one build with internal navigation, which is a real chunk of work on its own.

Given that, changelogs should go through **GitHub Releases** instead — no new infrastructure needed, and it's already half-built: `.claude/skills/generate-changelog` already ends by offering to run `gh release create [VERSION] --draft --notes '[SUMMARY]'`, and its own base-ref detection already defaults to `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` — the skill was written assuming tags would exist. Adopting this proposal completes something already designed, rather than adding something new. Run `/generate-changelog` at step 4 above (cutting the final tag) to produce the Release. A Pages-hosted changelog UI remains a legitimate future nice-to-have, just not the pragmatic starting point.

What changes vs. today
----------------------

|  | Today | Proposed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What gets deployed | A branch name, or an ad-hoc ref someone remembers | A named, immutable tag |
| Tracking "what's where" | Tribal knowledge / Slack history | GitHub Environments' Deployment history / `git tag -l` / GitHub Releases page |
| Can Test/SIT/UAT run independent cycles? | No — pointed at the same moving branch | Yes — each on its own tag |
| New infrastructure needed | — | A Test-tier P0 gate job (new); everything else — `deploy-test.yml`, tag protection, the version-guard, `npm version`, `/generate-changelog` — already exists or is a config change, not new code |

Open questions for the team
---------------------------

1. **Test gate design** — is deploy-then-gate (proposed above) acceptable, or should it match SIT's gate-then-deploy pattern exactly, at the cost of the fast on-demand deploy?
2. **Test gate scope** — P0 Playwright suite only, or should any of bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse also apply at this tier?
3. **SIT tag-triggering** GreenNew — review *(raised in review)* — this proposal's Flow diagram and per-environment table assume SIT redeploys when a new `-rc` tag is cut, but `deploy-sit.yml`'s real trigger today is `workflow_run` off `SIT Gate` completing on a `release/**` push, with no relationship to tag creation at all. Two options: (a) change `deploy-sit.yml` to trigger on a tag push instead, matching the Test/UAT/Stage/Prod model this proposal builds — a real workflow change, not just a docs update; or (b) keep SIT branch-triggered as-is and stop describing it as tag-scoped in this proposal, treating SIT as an intentional exception to the "every environment sits on a named tag" rule. Needs a decision before this proposal is considered final.",

    },
    "page_width": "full-width"
  }
}

SIT — Operational Details
-------------------------

SIT is a dedicated MRT environment for NewStore order management integration testing. It receives the same build as Digital Dev but points to a separate SFCC instance and has third-party integrations disabled (Einstein, Global-e, Narvar).

It is a **parallel lane** — it never gates the Digital release path. Digital Dev can proceed to release regardless of SIT status. The two lanes converge only at **STAGE**, where both Digital Dev green and NewStore OMS SIT complete are required before promotion. See the Environment Topology & Promotion Path page for the full six-tier model.

### Deployment

| Who deploys | How | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CI (GitHub Actions) | Automatic | After `sit-gate` passes on every `develop` push |
| Developer | Manual via `npm run push:sit && npm run activate:sit` | For hotfixes or out-of-band testing |

Manual deployments must use a `sit/*` or `hotfix/*` branch. Never push to SIT from `develop` or `main` without the CI gate having first confirmed Digital Dev is green.

### CI tagging

Every SIT deployment creates a `sit/deploy/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{sha}` git tag — NewStore uses this as the bundle reference when triaging integration failures. Sprint boundary tags (`sprint/{N}/{YYYY-MM-DD}`) are created automatically when `scripts/sprint.txt` is updated on a `develop` push.

### Critical rules

* **Never** direct production or UAT traffic to SIT.
* **Never** enable Einstein, Global-e, or Narvar on SIT — see `config/sit.js`.
* **Never** use SIT as a hotfix path to PROD. Hotfixes follow `hotfix/* → main → PROD`.
* If SIT is broken, **do not block** the Digital release — raise with the NewStore team independently.
* SIT SFCC credentials (`COMMERCE_API_*_SIT`) are separate from Digital Dev credentials — changing one set does not affect the other.

### Config

The environment override is at `config/sit.js`. It reads four environment variables set as GitHub Secrets: `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID_SIT`, `COMMERCE_API_ORG_ID_SIT`, `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE_SIT`, `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID_SIT`. MRT push credentials (`MRT_USER`, `MRT_API_KEY`) are shared with Digital Dev and scoped to the project slug in `mobify.config.js`.

### Rollback

If SIT serves a bad build, in order of speed:

1. **MRT Console rollback** — fastest: activate the previous bundle via the MRT Console UI. Previous bundle IDs are visible on the SIT environment page.
2. **Git tag revert** — identify the last good `sit/deploy/*` tag, check out that SHA, and run `npm run push:sit && npm run activate:sit` manually.
3. **CI re-run** — re-run the last successful `digital-sit.yml` workflow run that deployed a known-good build.

Option 1 is preferred. Contact the Integration Lead (#integration) if MRT Console access is needed in an emergency.

GitHub Branch Protection & CODEOWNERS Setup (one-time, ~15 minutes)
-------------------------------------------------------------------

Do this once when the repo is set up. The `protected-file-guard.yml` workflow and `CODEOWNERS` file do the detection — branch protection rules make them unmergeable when they fail.

### 1. Protect `develop`

Settings → Branches → Add branch protection rule → branch name pattern `develop`:

| Setting | Value | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Require a pull request before merging | ✅ On | No direct pushes to develop |
| Required approvals | **2** | One from owning squad, one cross-squad check |
| Dismiss stale reviews when new commits are pushed | ✅ On | Forces re-review after changes |
| Require review from Code Owners | ✅ On | Enforces CODEOWNERS — owner must approve |
| Require status checks to pass before merging | ✅ On | Blocks merge if Actions fail |
| Required status checks | `🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`, `🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning`, `🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check` | All four required |
| Require branches to be up to date before merging | ✅ On | Forces rebase on stale branches |
| Do not allow bypassing the above settings | ✅ On | **Admins cannot bypass — critical** |

### 2. Protect `main`

Same pattern as `develop`, plus: Required approvals **2** (both squad leads), Restrict who can push (Integration Lead + Squad Leads only), Do not allow bypassing.

### 3. Protect `release/*`

Required approvals **1**, require status checks to pass, restrict who can create matching branches to Squad Leads only.

### 4. Status check names

After the Actions workflow has run once, GitHub recognises the job names as available status checks. Exact strings to add:

Defaultnone🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check
🔴 Branch Target Check
🟡 Tier 2 — Protected Files Warning
🟡 Cross-Squad Boundary Check

### 5. Create GitHub Teams (required for CODEOWNERS)

Org → Teams → New Team:

| --- | --- | --- |
| Design System | `design-system` | UI Designer |

| Squad B Lead | `squad-b-lead` | Squad B tech lead |

Then update `CODEOWNERS`, replacing all `@your-org/` prefixes with the actual GitHub organisation slug.

### 6. Install CodeRabbit

Sign up at coderabbit.ai with the GitHub org account, install the CodeRabbit GitHub App on the repo — `coderabbit.yaml` at the repo root is picked up automatically. No additional GitHub Actions setup needed.

Branch protection rules
-----------------------

### `develop`

1. Require a pull request before merging
2. Required approvals: **2** (one from owning squad, one cross-squad check)
3. Require status checks to pass before merging — add check: `unit-tests` (from `qa.yml`)
4. Require branches to be up to date before merging
5. Do not allow bypassing the above settings

### `main`

1. Require a pull request before merging
2. Required approvals: **2** (both squad leads must approve release merges)
3. Require branches to be up to date before merging
4. Do not allow bypassing the above settings

Hotfix PRs into `main` still require 2 approvals — under deadline pressure, get the second approver on a call rather than bypassing the gate.

### `release/**`

Required check: `Digital SIT Gate` — composite job depending on all four SIT signal jobs.

| Signal | Tool | Threshold | Blocks? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Playwright P0 journeys | Playwright | 100% pass on P0 suite, all storefront configs | Yes |
| Lighthouse CI | LHCI | Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90, drop > 5 pts = blocked | Yes |
| MuleSoft contract tests | Pact / OpenAPI | Any schema breach = blocked | Yes (pending spec source confirmation) |
| Bundle size | bundlewatch | main.js < 180 kB, vendor.js < 250 kB, main.css < 50 kB | Yes |

Vitest and Storybook interaction + a11y tests run in `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`) — they gate the PR merge, not the environment deploy.

Configuring in GitHub: Settings → Branches → Add branch protection rule → branch pattern `release/**` → require status checks → add `Digital SIT Gate` → require branches up to date → do not allow bypassing (no admin overrides).

### STAGE convergence gate

STAGE promotion requires both the Digital SIT gate green and NewStore SIT to be complete. This is a **manual gate** enforced by the delivery team before raising a STAGE promotion PR, not an automated GitHub status check. Checklist before any STAGE PR:

* [ ] `Digital SIT Gate` check is green on the release branch
* [ ] NewStore team has confirmed SIT testing is complete for this sprint
* [ ] Integration Lead and both squad leads have signed off

### GitHub Pages — Playwright report publishing

Settings → Pages → set source to **GitHub Actions**. The Playwright HTML report publishes automatically to GitHub Pages on every push to `develop` once this is enabled.

Commit message quality enforcement
----------------------------------

Enforced at two layers:

**Layer 1 — local** `commit-msg` **hook** (Husky-installed via `npm install`). Rejects commits not matching `type(optional-scope): short description`. Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`, `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `upstream-sync`. Merge commits, reverts, fixups, squash commits, and WIP prefixes pass through automatically.

**Layer 2 — CodeRabbit PR review** (`coderabbit.yaml`). Checks every commit in every PR for conventional commits compliance, catching commits pushed without the local hook installed.

This matters because the changelog skill (`/generate-changelog`) parses commit history by conventional type to produce the four-audience release changelog — non-conventional commits are classified "Uncategorised" and can't be automatically routed.

`hotfix/*` branch has ever existed in zimmermann-pwa — confirmed via `gh api
repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches` (only `develop`, `main`, and several `feature/*`/`fix/*`),

   SFCC foundations and deliver the global UI shell with homepage ready for the next build phase")
   ran 2026-07-06 → **closed 2026-07-26**. **SFCC Sprint 2 is active now**, 2026-07-28 → 2026-08-10.
   Sprint 3 starts 2026-08-10. **`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`'s sprint table is stale/wrong** —
   it's a 2026-06-23 draft that still labels "Current position" as "Sprint 0," and its dates
   (Sprint 1 = 29 Jun–10 Jul, Sprint 3 = 27 Jul–7 Aug) don't match the real Jira board by several
   days. Don't cite sprintScope.md's dates for real sprint boundaries — pull the live board instead.
2. **Sprint 1 already closed calendar-wise, but the epic that owns platform/CI-CD setup did not
   close with it.** `SFCC-1` ("Platform Setup & Environments," explicit scope includes "CI/CD
   pipeline including... bundle size gate, Playwright P0 suite, Lighthouse CI") is **still "In
   Progress"**, last updated today. That's the substantive reason no release branch got cut at
   Sprint 1's close — the foundation work the Branching Guide's "when a sprint is complete" trigger
   assumes was ready, wasn't actually done yet.
3. **The concrete blockers are tracked and still open**, not hidden: Confluence "[7.1c CI/CD &
   Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530)"
   (v2) lists "Configure `release/**` branch protection" as **⬜, owner Integration Lead**, plus a
   long list of still-⬜ SIT-environment items (GitHub `sit` environment not created, `MRT_SIT_URL`/
   `COMMERCE_API_*_SIT` secrets unset, MRT project slug unconfirmed in `mobify.config.js`).

   TEST, SIT & UAT for All Storefronts," Sprint 2 ticket, In Progress) got a comment today
   (2026-08-03 20:17, Victor T. Crisostomo): *"Deployment done on UAT. Core/Vendor data imported...
   Sample data and MRT working on test environment. Checking on SIT MRT environment."* — i.e. SIT
   MRT still isn't confirmed working as of this afternoon. Five follow-on tickets (SFCC-259..263,
   "Deploy to UAT: Base Category/Pricebook/Product Catalogue/Inventory List/8 Storefronts Setup")
   are queued **To Do**, blocked on SFCC-254 — but these are **SFCC/Business-Manager config
   deployments** (a different backend repo/process), not this PWA repo's `release/*` branch flow.
   Easy to conflate the two if a scrum master hears "deploying to UAT" from the SFCC side.
5. **Confluence "[Branching Guide (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/304840733)"**
   (v3, canonical source AGENTS.md/`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md` are built from) says release
   branches are "created by squad leads or CI from a tagged `develop` state... developers do not
   create these," tagged via **`scripts/tagRelease.sh`** (exists in repo, confirmed) run from `main`
   *after* the release PR merges (creates both `v{version}` and `release/digital/v{version}` tags).
   Separately, `deploy-dev.yml` has a dormant **`tag-sprint`** job that auto-tags `sprint/{N}/{date}`
   whenever `scripts/sprint.txt` changes on `develop` — **but `scripts/sprint.txt` doesn't exist in
   the repo yet**, so this has never fired either (`git tag -l` confirms zero `sprint/*` tags). If
   the scrum master expected *some* automatic tag/branch to appear at a sprint boundary, this
   inert-but-wired mechanism is a plausible source of that expectation.
6. **Open, unresolved decision that should land before the first release branch is cut:** draft
   Confluence proposal "[Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656)"
   (v18, still "Draft — for review by squad leads + Integration lead," still has an unresolved
   Open Question 3 about whether `deploy-sit.yml` becomes tag-triggered) would **replace**
   `scripts/tagRelease.sh` with `npm version`-based tagging entirely. Deciding this first avoids
   cutting the first real release under a tagging convention that gets retired a sprint later.

**How to apply:** If asked again whether the release branch exists/is "already set up" — answer is
still **no**. Frame it as *on track, not overdue*: the Branching Guide's own trigger ("sprint
complete + something ready to promote") hasn't fully fired yet, because the epic that delivers the
prerequisites (`SFCC-1`) is still open, and the concrete missing pieces (release/** branch
protection, SIT secrets/environment, `mobify.config.js`) are already tracked on 7.1c owned by
Integration Lead, not undiscovered gaps. Natural next checkpoint is Sprint 2's close (2026-08-10) —
*if* the 7.1c SIT-environment items land before then. Re-verify via `gh api
repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/branches`, `git tag -l`, and the current Jira sprint board
(`board 500`) before restating any of this — it changes fast. See also
[[project_coverage_threshold]] for the separate-repo distinction this finding leans on again (PWA
repo vs. SFCC/BM backend repo).

---
name: project-env-topology-doc-conflicts
description: "Live contradictions between Confluence env-topology docs and the actual zimmermann-pwa deploy pipeline (verified 2026-08-05)"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Verified 2026-08-05 against the real `.github/workflows/` + `gh` API. Several docs disagree with each other and with the code. Flag these (doc-integrity rule) before wiring release/promotion tooling; do not silently pick one.

1. **Test tier existence.** Confluence "Environment Topology & Promotion Path" (page 304840708, v4) describes a 6-tier model **with no Test tier** (LOCAL→DEV→SIT→STAGE→UAT→PROD). But `.docs/architecture.md`, 05.6 Environment Details (285540356), the tag proposal (335216656), SFCC-254, and the **actual `deploy-test.yml` + `test` GitHub Environment** all include a Test tier. The topology page is stale on this.

2. **Promotion order (Stage vs UAT).** Topology page 304840708 orders **STAGE → UAT** (Stage = convergence, then UAT business acceptance). `.docs/architecture.md` and the tag proposal order **UAT → STAGE → PROD**. Genuinely different sequencing — needs a team decision; affects promotion tooling.

3. **SIT trigger model.** Topology page + 05.6 say SIT **auto-deploys on every `develop` push** after sit-gate. Reality: `deploy-sit.yml` triggers on `workflow_run` of **"SIT Gate" (digital-sit.yml) completing on `release/**`** — SIT is release-branch-driven, not develop-driven. `.docs/memory/projectState.md` has this right; the Confluence pages don't. (This is the tag proposal's still-open Question 3.)

4. **GitHub Environment names.** Topology page's secret-scope table names `pre-prod` and `production`; the **actual** environments are `staging` and `prod`. `deploy-stg.yml` binds `environment: staging` (filename says `stg`); `deploy-prod.yml` binds `prod` but the MRT push target is `production`. Version-guard/promotion tooling must key off the real names (`dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod`) — the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once (commit 12bf91b).

5. **CI/CD architecture stale.** "PWA CI/CD Pipeline" (305561601) and "7.1c Checklist" (305430530) describe `deploy-sit` as a **job inside `digital-sit.yml`** and list the `sit` environment + MRT secrets as not-yet-created. Reality: separate `deploy-*.yml` workflows, and all six environments exist. 7.1c/305561601 need a refresh.

6. **`mobify.config.js` referenced but absent.** frozenFiles.md (Tier 1), `protected-file-guard.yml`/`qa.yml` path filters, `architecture.md`, and 7.1c all reference `mobify.config.js` — the file **does not exist**. `package.json` has no `mobify` key (uses `ccExtensibility`). MRT config actually lives in `config/default.js` `ssrParameters`. Verify where the MRT project slug for `pwa-kit-dev push` actually resolves from.

**How to apply:** When advising on release/deploy topology, trust the code + `gh` live state over the Confluence topology pages; treat 304840708/305561601/7.1c as needing updates. The repo SSOT for topology is `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md §14.1` (via `architecture.md`). See [[project-release-branch-status]].

content.text:
Here's the full in-depth readiness check for **(1) standing up the first `release/*` branch** and **(2) getting all environments deployed**, cross-referenced across the codebase, Confluence, and JIRA. (SFCC-237 set aside as a non-blocker per your note.)

## Bottom line

The infrastructure is **far more built-out than the Confluence docs claim** — all six per-tier deploy workflows and all six GitHub Environments already exist, and you personally hold `tier-1-approvers` + repo `admin`, so you can do every infra step without an external approver. The gating gaps are concentrated in three places: **the SIT Gate can't pass yet** (so creating the release branch won't produce a SIT deploy), **prod is entirely unconfigured**, and **the tag/version-promotion layer is still proposal-only**. None are large, but they must be closed in the right order.

## JIRA landscape — mind the scope boundary

| Ticket | Type / Status | What it really is |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-254** *(your reference)* | Task · In Progress · assignee **Victor T. Crisostomo** | "Environment Setup DEV/TEST/SIT/UAT for All Storefronts" — **SFCC Business-Manager + data-seeding** work. Blocks SFCC-259→263 (BM category/pricebook/catalogue/inventory/8-storefronts). **Blocked-by SFCC-126** (Global Customer List Setup — status *Blocked*). |
| Its comments (Aug 3–4) | — | Victor: *"Deployment done on UAT. Core/Vendor data imported. Sample data + MRT working on test. Checking SIT MRT."* → *"[you] will work on SIT deployment for MRT."* |
| Parent **SFCC-1** | Epic · In Progress | "Platform Setup & Environments" — owns the CI/CD pipeline scope. |

**Scope flag:** SFCC-254 as written is Victor's SFCC-side environment/data setup. Your remit — the **PWA-Kit release branch + MRT deploy pipeline** — overlaps but isn't cleanly captured by it. Its AC self-marks DEV/TEST/UAT "done", but that's the SFCC BM/org side; on the MRT side only the **DEV storefront grid is populated** (05.6), Test/SIT/UAT grids are empty. Worth agreeing whether your work sits as a linked story under SFCC-1 rather than inside SFCC-254, so ownership is unambiguous.

## What's already in place (green)

- **6 deploy workflows, all active:** Deploy Dev/Test/SIT/STG/UAT/PROD, + SIT Gate, QA, Protected File Guard, Sync Env Vars to MRT, Upstream Release Watch, Weekly Agents.
- **6 GitHub Environments exist:** `dev, test, sit, uat, staging, prod` (+ `shared`, `github-pages`).
- **MRT + SFCC orgs provisioned** for every tier (05.6 has URLs + org IDs).
- **Per-tier config wired:** `config/{dev,test,sit,uat,staging,production}.js` + `push:{dev,test,sit,staging,uat,prod}` scripts + `switchEnv.mjs` supporting all six tiers.
- **MRT auth present** as repo-level secrets (`MRT_USER`, `MRT_API_KEY`), inherited by all envs.
- **You can self-serve the infra:** `marcelannavarro` is 1 of 2 `tier-1-approvers` and repo `admin` → can run `npm run env -- push`, create rulesets/branch protection, and cut final tags.

## Goal 1 — Release branch: readiness & gaps

Creating `release/v0.1.0` will be the **first `release/*` branch ever**, which is significant: it's the event that **first activates the entire SIT lane** (SIT Gate on push/PR to `release/**` → `deploy-sit` on gate success). That lane has never run.

**Blockers before the SIT lane goes green:**

| Gap | Detail | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 🔴 **LHCI secrets unset** | `LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT` not set at repo or env level | `lighthouse-ci` job fails → `sit-gate` fails → **`deploy-sit` never fires** |
| 🔴 **E2E data unset** | `RETAIL_APP_HOME`, `PWA_E2E_USER_*`, `E2E_*_PRODUCT_SKU`, `BROWSERSTACK_*` absent (repo variables list is empty) | `playwright-p0` in the gate has no target/data |
| 🟡 **`release/**` branch protection not configured** | 7.1c ⬜ (owner Integration Lead); required check should be `Digital SIT Gate`, restrict-creation to squad leads | Nothing enforces the gate on release PRs yet |
| 🟢 **`test:contracts` is a stub** | `echo … && exit 0` | Harmless — passes the gate as designed |

**Tag/versioning layer is proposal-only:** zero tags anywhere, `package.json` still `0.0.1`, no `npm version` adoption, no version-guard/downgrade check in any `deploy-*.yml`, no tag ruleset. `scripts/tagRelease.sh` exists but creates a **different, conflicting** scheme (`v{ver}` + `release/digital/v{ver}`) that the tag-based-promotion proposal says to retire.

## Goal 2 — Deploy all environments: per-tier state

| Env | Deploy trigger | Config present? | Ready to deploy? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **dev** | auto (push→`develop`) | ✅ COMMERCE_API_* + CONTENTFUL_* + SHORT_CODE/SITE_ID | ✅ (only tier with storefronts live) |
| **test** | `workflow_dispatch` (ref=develop) | ✅ | ⚠️ push works; storefront grid empty |
| **sit** | `workflow_run` off SIT Gate on `release/**` | ✅ | ⚠️ needs release branch + green gate first |
| **uat** | `workflow_dispatch` (ref=develop) | ✅ | ⚠️ push works; storefront grid empty |
| **staging** | `workflow_dispatch` (ref=main) | ✅ | ⚠️ push works |
| **prod** | `workflow_dispatch` (ref required) | 🔴 **EMPTY — no vars, no secrets** | 🔴 build would run with no Commerce/Contentful config |

**Cross-cutting deploy gaps:**
- 🔴 **prod environment is completely unconfigured** — no `COMMERCE_API_*`, no `CONTENTFUL_*`. That's expected (prod comes last, needs real prod creds + your tier-1 push), but it's the biggest single gap for "all environments deployed."
- 🟡 **Push ≠ activate.** `push:*` only runs `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`; there are **no `activate:*` scripts**, yet 05.6 tells devs to run `npm run push:sit && npm run activate:sit`. Confirm the activation path (MRT auto-deploy on push, MRT console, or scripts to add) before calling a tier "deployed."
- 🟡 **Security smell:** `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET` is stored as a **plaintext env Variable** on test/sit/uat/staging (it's also a repo Secret). A `*_SECRET` as a Variable isn't masked — verify it should be a Secret only. (Same class as the [PR #42 env-sync gotcha](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656).)
- 🟡 **`stg`≠`staging` naming trap:** `deploy-stg.yml` binds `environment: staging`; `deploy-prod.yml` binds `prod` but MRT target is `production`. Any promotion/version-guard tooling must map to the real env names — this exact mismatch bit the repo once (commit `12bf91b`).

## Documentation contradictions to reconcile (doc-integrity flags)

The Confluence env docs have drifted from the code. Per project rules I'm flagging, not resolving:

1. **Test tier:** "Environment Topology & Promotion Path" (304840708) shows a 6-tier model with **no Test tier**; the code, 05.6, architecture.md and SFCC-254 all include Test.
2. **Promotion order:** topology page orders **Stage → UAT**; `architecture.md` + the tag proposal order **UAT → Stage → Prod**. Genuine disagreement — needs a team decision.
3. **SIT trigger:** topology page + 05.6 say SIT auto-deploys **on every `develop` push**; reality is `deploy-sit` fires from the **SIT Gate completing on `release/**`**. (`projectState.md` is correct.)
4. **Env names:** topology page names `pre-prod`/`production`; actual are `staging`/`prod`.
5. **Stale CI/CD pages:** "PWA CI/CD Pipeline" (305561601) + "7.1c Checklist" (305430530) describe `deploy-sit` as a *job inside `digital-sit.yml`* and the `sit` env + secrets as not-yet-created — both outdated.
6. **`mobify.config.js`** is referenced by frozenFiles.md (Tier 1), the guard workflows, architecture.md and 7.1c — but **the file doesn't exist** (no `mobify` key in package.json either). Verify where the MRT project slug actually resolves from.

## Decisions that need team sign-off before you cut the first release

1. **Adopt the tag-based promotion model** (proposal 335216656) or keep `tagRelease.sh`? This determines your very first tag's format (`v0.1.0-rc.0` vs `v0.1.0`). Cutting the first release under a scheme that's retired a sprint later is the thing to avoid.
2. **Stage↔UAT order** (contradiction #2 above).
3. **The tag proposal's Open Question 3** — does `deploy-sit.yml` become tag-triggered, or stay `workflow_run`-off-the-gate? The AGENTS.md/governance edits in that proposal need both squad leads + Integration lead.

## Recommended sequence

1. **Unblock the SIT gate first** (LHCI secrets + E2E data secrets, + `release/**` branch protection with `Digital SIT Gate` required) — otherwise the release branch produces a red lane on day one.
2. **Lock the tagging decision** (proposal vs `tagRelease.sh`) with the squad/Integration leads, since it dictates the first tag.
3. **Cut `release/v0.1.0`** from `develop`, let SIT Gate run → SIT deploy.
4. **Populate + deploy the manual tiers** in order (test → uat → staging), then **configure prod** (vars + secrets via your `env push`) last.
5. **Reconcile the stale Confluence topology/CI-CD pages** to match reality.

I've saved the verified live-state and the doc conflicts to project memory so this doesn't have to be re-derived next session.

Want me to go deeper on any branch of this — e.g. draft the exact `release/**` branch-protection + tag-ruleset config, produce the prod-env variable checklist, or write up the Confluence reconciliation? I'll hold on making any changes until you point me at one.

file.content:
name: SIT Gate

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  playwright-p0:
    name: Playwright P0 journeys
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Install Playwright browsers
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Run P0 suite
        run: node_modules/.bin/playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github
        env:
          RETAIL_APP_HOME: ${{ vars.RETAIL_APP_HOME }}

      - name: Upload Playwright report
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: playwright-report
          path: playwright-report/
          retention-days: 30

      - name: Upload Pages artifact
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: playwright-report/

  deploy-playwright-report:
    name: Publish Playwright report to Pages
    needs: playwright-p0
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4

  lighthouse-ci:
    name: Lighthouse CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    env:
      LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL }}
      LHCI_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TOKEN }}
      LHCI_TARGET_URL: ${{ secrets.LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Run Lighthouse CI
        run: node_modules/.bin/lhci autorun

      - name: Upload Lighthouse results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: lighthouse-results
          path: .lighthouseci/
          retention-days: 30

  contract-tests:
    name: MuleSoft contract tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      # TODO: Replace with real contract assertion once MuleSoft publishes OpenAPI specs.
      # Owner: Zimmermann integration team + Accenture delivery lead to align.
      - name: Run contract tests
        run: npm run test:contracts

  bundle-size:
    name: Bundle size check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Build and check bundle size
        run: npm run test:max-file-size

  sit-gate:
    name: SIT Gate
    needs: [playwright-p0, lighthouse-ci, contract-tests, bundle-size]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check all SIT signals passed
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}" != "success" ] || \
             [ "${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "SIT gate: one or more checks failed"
            echo "  playwright-p0:   ${{ needs.playwright-p0.result }}"
            echo "  lighthouse-ci:   ${{ needs.lighthouse-ci.result }}"
            echo "  contract-tests:  ${{ needs.contract-tests.result }}"
            echo "  bundle-size:     ${{ needs.bundle-size.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "SIT gate: all checks passed"

name: Deploy SIT

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['SIT Gate']
    types:
      - completed
    branches:
      - 'release/**'

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  deploy-sit:
    name: Deploy to SIT
    if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: sit
    env:
      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install --include=dev

      - name: Push build to SIT
        run: npm run push:sit

content.text:
Read both — now I can give you exact requirements. The key insight: **creating the branch is trivial; making its SIT gate go green is the actual work.** And good news — **the whole "how do we tag releases" debate does *not* block this part.** SIT deploy uses the commit SHA, not a tag, so we can get the release branch + SIT working today without waiting on that decision.

Here's what "up and running" actually needs.

## What the SIT gate is made of

When you push `release/v0.1.0`, the **"SIT Gate"** workflow runs 4 checks. Their real status today:

| Check | Needs | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **contract-tests** | nothing (it's a stub that passes) | ✅ already green |
| **bundle-size** | just builds the app | ✅ should pass |
| **playwright-p0** | `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable + SIT actually serving a storefront | 🔴 URL unset |
| **lighthouse-ci** | a Lighthouse server + 3 secrets (`LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL`, `LHCI_TOKEN`, `LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT`) | 🔴 all unset |

If all 4 are green, the **SIT deploy fires automatically** (`npm run push:sit`, using MRT creds that already exist). So the gate is the whole ballgame.

## What we need, in three buckets

**Bucket 1 — we can do ourselves (you're admin):**
1. Create + push `release/v0.1.0` from `develop`.
2. Set the `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable to the SIT URL (we already have it from the 05.6 doc — `zimmermann-sit…exp-delivery.com`).
3. Turn on `release/**` branch protection with the required check.

**Bucket 2 — one manual "seeding" step:**
4. Do a one-time manual `npm run push:sit` so SIT is actually serving a storefront. This solves a chicken-and-egg: the gate *tests* SIT, but the auto-deploy only runs *after* the gate passes — so the very first SIT deploy has to be manual. After that, the gate→deploy loop is self-sustaining.

**Bucket 3 — the one real external dependency:**
5. The **Lighthouse CI server + its 3 secrets** — this is DevOps/IT, not you. Until it exists, `lighthouse-ci` can't pass, so the gate stays red. This is the single thing that can hold up a *fully green* gate today.

## Three exact gotchas worth knowing

- **The required check is literally named `SIT Gate`** — not "Digital SIT Gate" like 7.1c/Confluence say. Use the real name.
- **You can only add it as a required check *after* it's run once.** So the order is: create branch → first push triggers "SIT Gate" → *then* add it to branch protection.
- **Creating the branch is safe even if the gate is red** — nothing deploys unless the gate passes. So we lose nothing by cutting it now and lighting up the checks to see exactly what's missing.

## Proposed first move

The cleanest start is: **cut `release/v0.1.0` and push it**, which triggers the first-ever "SIT Gate" run and shows us live which checks pass. Then we set branch protection, set `RETAIL_APP_HOME`, and chase the Lighthouse server with DevOps.

Before I push anything, two quick confirmations:

1. **Branch name — `release/v0.1.0`?** (Matches the pre-launch "start at v0.1.0" decision. Say the word if you want a different version.)
2. **OK to create it from the current `develop` and push it to origin?** It's a real remote push on a supervised branch, so I want your explicit go before I do it.

content.thinking:
I'm pulling together a comparison between the tag-based promotion model from the Confluence proposal and what's actually running in the current workflows. I have the proposal details, the real workflow inventory from the Explore agent, and the actual workflow files to work from, so I can map out how they align, where the gaps are, and what the tradeoffs look like. The current state has no tags yet, with package.json at 0.0.1 and an existing tagRelease script that creates raw git tags. The proposal pushes for immutable semantic version tags (vX.Y.Z-rc.N for RCs, vX.Y.Z for final releases, vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N for hotfixes) using npm version instead, starting at v0.1.0 pre-launch and bumping minor per sprint until v1.0.0 at go-live. The key shift is replacing branch-based deploys with tag-based refs in the workflow_dispatch inputs across test/uat/stg/prod, though SIT remains workflow_run-triggered which creates a complication.

I'm now looking at the version-guard logic that needs to sit in each deploy workflow — it'll fetch the currently deployed tag via the Deployments API, compare versions semantically, and block any downgrade attempts, with a mapping layer to translate tier names to environment names. GitHub Rulesets will enforce tag protection in two layers: one allowing RC tag creation and immutability, another restricting final and hotfix tags to tier-1 approvers only, backed up by a push validation workflow. The old tagRelease.sh gets retired while sprint/* tags coexist in their own namespace, and changelog generation hooks into the existing GitHub Releases mechanism.

I need to document this in a new tagging.md governance file and update the AGENTS.md branch table, both requiring squad-lead and Integration-lead approval. Deployment tracking will use the GitHub Environments Deployments API which is already available. There are still some open questions around test gate sequencing, scope, and how SIT should trigger on tags.

Now I'm structuring a comparison between the current state and this proposal across multiple dimensions, then identifying gaps, benefits, and risks. I also need to account for a test tier gate that doesn't exist yet, plus governance mechanisms like rulesets and a validation workflow. Looking at the concrete gaps: we're currently shipping with a static version in package.json and no tags, the deploy workflows accept a ref but skip any version validation, there's no ruleset enforcement around tag creation, tagRelease.sh is creating conflicting tag formats that need to be retired, and SIT's workflow_run trigger complicates the ref-passing story.

The test tier has a dispatch workflow but no gate—the proposal adds a P0 gate as a new job. We're also missing changelog and release automation wired together, governance docs need to be written and signed off, and while the Deployments API is available, it's not being surfaced to the team. The proposal's main advantage is immutability and permanence through tags, though there's an architectural mismatch with how SIT currently triggers.

The benefits are clear: environments can decouple onto different tags for independent test cycles, downgrade protection prevents accidents, and we get a solid audit trail through annotated tags and the Deployments API. It's standard GitFlow/SemVer that most teams recognize, reuses existing infrastructure, and enforces consistency server-side through rulesets rather than relying on convention alone. The main trade-off is adding more process overhead.

On the downside, developers need to learn the npm version prerelease flow for each promotion, and there's a real tension with SIT — it's currently driven by release branches and workflow runs, not tags, so either we change deploy-sit.yml or accept it as an exception that breaks the "every env on a tag" story. The version-guard logic has some sharp edges too: tier-to-env name mapping, fail-closed semantics, and semver prerelease comparison can be subtle to get right. We'd also need two separate rulesets due to GitHub's bypass limitations, and any governance changes require sign-off from squad and integration leads, which slows things down.

npm version does add release-branch commits and a tag, which is a behavior change, and retiring tagRelease.sh means migrating the Branching Guide — there's transition risk. The proposal also doesn't directly address the deploy-push-versus-activate question or why prod is empty, though people might assume it does. I'm noticing some claims in the proposal don't quite match reality — it says all deploy-*.yml workflows take a ref via dispatch, but SIT doesn't — so that needs fixing before we move forward.

For the immediate release-branch work, the proposal isn't a blocker for SIT. We can cut release/v0.1.0 and get SIT green using SHA-based deploys right now; the tag model only matters when we promote to Test, UAT, Stage, and Prod. That said, if we're about to start those manual-tier promotions soon, it's worth deciding the tag convention first to avoid doing the first promotion under a rule that then changes. There's a window here: we can create the branch and run SIT now, then lock in the tag model before the first UAT promotion. Adopting the proposal itself requires sign-off. The current approach is simpler but leaves real gaps—no protection against branch deletion, environments locked together, no downgrade safeguards, no audit trail. For the scale we're operating at (multi-region, per-sprint cadence, eight storefronts), the tag-based model is the right standard. I'd recommend adopting it in phases: build the tooling first (version automation and rulesets), resolve the SIT work in Q3, then tackle governance docs. It's not blocking today's work, but it's the direction we should move.

Now I need to structure this as a technical comparison—the user asked explicitly for gaps, pros, cons, and implications, so I'll give them a substantive analysis with a clear recommendation, not an oversimplified version. I'll use a comparison table to make it scannable, then call out where the proposal's claims don't match reality, especially around the SIT trigger and the assumption that deploy equals push-only.

content.text:
Good question to settle before we promote anything. Here's how the proposal stacks up against what's actually in the repo today — grounded in the real workflows, not the proposal's own description of them (which is slightly off in a couple of places I'll flag).

## Side-by-side

| Dimension | Current implementation | Proposed (335216656) |
|---|---|---|
| **What gets deployed** | An arbitrary `ref` you type into a `workflow_dispatch` (branch name, SHA, whatever someone remembers) | A named, **immutable tag** (`v0.1.0-rc.1`, `v0.1.0`) |
| **Dev** | Auto on every `develop` merge (`deploy-dev`) | Unchanged (correct as-is) |
| **Test** | `workflow_dispatch`, default ref `develop`, **no gate** | Same trigger + a **new P0-only gate** after deploy |
| **SIT** | `workflow_run` off "SIT Gate" completing on `release/**`, deploys the gate's SHA | Proposed to redeploy on each new `-rc` tag — **but this is unresolved** (Open Q3) |
| **UAT / Stage / Prod** | `workflow_dispatch`, manual ref (uat→develop, stg→main, prod→required) | Same trigger, but ref = a specific tag |
| **Env cadence independence** | Lockstep — envs pointed at the same moving branch can't run separate cycles | Each env can sit on a **different tag** simultaneously |
| **Downgrade protection** | **None** — you can deploy an older ref over a newer one, silently | `semver` version-guard step, fails on downgrade |
| **Tag creation** | `scripts/tagRelease.sh` (raw `git tag`, `v{ver}` + `release/digital/v{ver}`, from `main`) — **never used, 0 tags exist** | `npm version` (annotated tags), enforced by 2 GitHub Rulesets |
| **"What's live where"** | Tribal / Slack | GitHub Deployments API + Releases page (both already free) |
| **`package.json` version** | Static `0.0.1` | Tracks the release automatically via `npm version` |

## Gaps to close (current → proposed)

1. **No tagging at all** → adopt `npm version`; first tag `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
2. **No version-guard** in any `deploy-*.yml` → add a semver downgrade check (with the `stg→staging` env-name mapping and fail-closed logic).
3. **No tag rulesets / no `push: tags:` validation workflow** → add 2 rulesets (RC open + immutable; final/hotfix restricted to tier-1) plus a validation workflow.
4. **`tagRelease.sh` conflicts** with the `npm version` scheme → retire it.
5. **SIT doesn't fit the tag model** → SIT is `workflow_run`-driven off the gate, *not* dispatch/tag-driven. This is the proposal's own Open Q3 and a real architectural mismatch, not a doc tweak.
6. **Test tier has no gate** → add the P0 gate job.
7. **Governance docs unwritten** (`AGENTS.md` branch table, a `tagging.md`) → needs sign-off.

## Pros of the proposal

- **Solves the actual problem:** PR branches get deleted on merge — a tag survives, so you can always answer "what shipped to SIT on the 5th." Tags decouple env cadences (the core pain).
- **Downgrade protection** — the current model has *zero* guardrails against clobbering a newer deploy with an older ref.
- **Real audit trail** for a multi-env, multi-region, 8-storefront, per-sprint cadence — this is the standard GitFlow/SemVer answer, not a bespoke one.
- **Mostly reuses what exists** — `deploy-*.yml`, `generate-changelog`'s `gh release create`, the Deployments API. It's config + a guard step, not a rebuild.
- **Server-side enforcement** (rulesets) matters here specifically because this repo is heavily Claude-assisted — a rule doc alone won't stop a malformed tag; a ruleset will.

## Cons / risks / sharp edges

- **The SIT mismatch is unresolved.** Either change `deploy-sit.yml` from `workflow_run`→tag-push (a real workflow change with its own testing), or accept SIT as an exception to "every env sits on a tag" — which dents the model's clean story. Must be decided, not hand-waved.
- **The version-guard is fiddly to get right:** tier→env name mapping (`stg`≠`staging`, `prod` env vs `production` MRT target), fail-closed on API errors, and SemVer pre-release comparison (`rc.10` vs `rc.2` breaks with naive string compare). Needs the `semver` package and actual testing — a hand-rolled version will bite.
- **Two rulesets, not one** (GitHub's single-bypass-list limit) → more config surface to maintain.
- **Process overhead** — a tag at each promotion, and devs learning the `npm version prerelease/preminor/graduate` flow. Small, but a behavior change (each tag also adds a commit to the release branch).
- **Governance is the slow part** — `AGENTS.md` changes need both squad leads *and* the Integration lead (stronger than the usual Tier-1 rule). You + Tim are the two tier-1-approvers, so it's reachable, but it's a sign-off, not a merge-and-go.
- **Transition confusion** — the current Branching Guide still prescribes `tagRelease.sh`; retiring it mid-flight risks people following stale docs.
- **The proposal has a factual error to fix first:** it claims "every `deploy-*.yml` already takes a `ref` via `workflow_dispatch`" — SIT doesn't. Correct that before anyone implements from it.
- **Doesn't touch** the two things people will conflate it with: prod being empty, and push-vs-activate. Orthogonal, but worth stating so scope stays clean.

## Implications

- **For the release-branch work we're about to do: none — it's not a prerequisite.** SIT deploys off the commit SHA and Dev is automatic, so we can cut `release/v0.1.0` and get the SIT gate green today with **zero tags**. The tag model only starts mattering at the **first manual promotion to UAT** (and Stage/Prod). So there's a clean window: do the branch + SIT now, decide tags before the first UAT push.
- **Adopt-in-phases is the low-regret path** — and the proposal already splits it that way. The **tooling** (`npm version`, rulesets, version-guard) is "safe to build now, touches no governance." The **governance docs** are the gated part. You can bank the high-value guardrails before the sign-off meeting.
- **The highest-value pieces are the version-guard + rulesets**, not the tag naming itself — they're what stop a bad prod deploy. If you only did one thing from this proposal, it'd be those.

## My recommendation

**Adopt it — it's the right model for this project's shape — but sequence it:** (1) create the release branch + get SIT green now (no tags needed); (2) before the first UAT promotion, lock the naming + build the tooling half (npm version, 2 rulesets, version-guard) and **resolve the SIT Open-Q3**; (3) take the governance-doc changes to the leads last. Don't cut the first *final* tag until the naming decision is signed off, or you'll re-tag under a new scheme a sprint later.

content.text:
Direct answer: **No — creating the release branch does not depend on deploying the environments.** If anything, the dependency runs the *other* way.

## Why

Creating `release/v0.1.0` is just a git branch off `develop` and a push. Nothing about that git action needs any environment to be deployed — and all the environments (GitHub, MRT, SFCC orgs) already *exist* regardless.

The one place branches and deployments touch is the **SIT gate**, and there the arrow points **branch → deployment**, not the reverse:

- Pushing the release branch is what **triggers** the "SIT Gate" workflow (it only runs on `release/**`).
- If the gate goes green, **it** triggers the SIT deploy.

So the release branch is the thing that *switches the SIT lane on* — it's upstream of the deployment, not waiting behind it.

## The one nuance (and it's SIT-only, not "all environments")

For the gate to actually go **green**, its two live checks (`playwright-p0`, `lighthouse-ci`) need a storefront *serving* at the SIT URL to test against. That's the small chicken-and-egg I mentioned: the gate tests SIT, but the auto-deploy runs *after* the gate — so the very first time, SIT needs one manual `push:sit` to seed it.

But note what that dependency is and isn't:

- It's **one tier (SIT)**, not "deploy all environments."
- It's about making the gate **green**, not about **creating** the branch.
- It happens **after** the branch exists, alongside it — not as a prerequisite.
- UAT / Stage / Prod deploys, and the tag-promotion decision, are all **downstream** of this — none of them gate the branch.

## So for sequencing

We can create the release branch **now**, independently. The only two things to line up *alongside* it (not before it) to get a fully green gate are: the one-time SIT seed, and the Lighthouse server from DevOps. Everything else waits its turn.

That keeps this clean and decoupled from the tag decision, exactly as you wanted.
